creatures.name: selachian-ursine-stalker
creatures.source: The chimeric shark-bear quadruped drawn in graphite in the center of IMAGE 1
creatures.pose: A stalking quadruped stance with arched furred back, white shark head angled three-quarters down to the left, and long caudal fin sweeping across the lower flank.
creatures.why: It is the sole monumental predator depicted in IMAGE 1, combining shark cranial architecture with heavily furred bear limbs.

shape.summary: A chunky chimera with a heavy grey-furred quadruped torso, a smooth ivory shark hood and dorsal fin, and a sweeping tail blade.

legend.R: raised ground (plateau, one or more blocks above G)

composition.mass: Visual weight sits heavily on the central raised plateau tiers (rows 4 to 6) where the massive torso and predatory skull loom.
composition.read: The viewer enters from the south across stepped graphite-shard path tiles, moving between framing bristle clusters. The path leads directly to the cleft at the foot of the raised stone plateau where the chimera stalker holds its hunting crouch, its caudal fin sweeping low to frame the right foreground.

lighting.notes: pale paper glare with heavy graphite core drop: Captures the stark contrast between the luminous off-white paper matrix and the dense, light-absorbing graphite shadow deposits.

rules: Confine bristle clumps to the peripheral flanks and plateau lips.
Keep the central prowling arena clear of tall props to emphasize the creature's silhouette.
Orient shard slabs along the fracture axes of the stepped plateaus.

lens.aspect: medium.marks and medium.surface: translates dense graphite cross-hatching, sharp pencil contour lines, and raw sketch paper tooth into fractured slate slabs and bristled terrain.
lens.place: A wind-scoured graphite moraine of fractured paper slate and bristle quills.
lens.summary: A fragmented shard plateau sculpted from dense graphite hatching lines, holding a prowling shark-bear titan atop layered slate terraces.
lens.differs: Replaces soft organic turf with pale paper-sand plates and sharp charcoal shale cliffs, emphasizing hard strokes and fibrous quill clusters.

shaper.name: shards
shaper.why: Reflects the crisp, high-pressure pencil hatching and faceted contour marks that fracture the blank sketch page into dynamic angular planes.

surface_mix.why: Mimics the tooth of paper ground (sand) broken by rubbed graphite smudges (dirt) and hardened slate core deposits (stone).

cliff_treatment.why: Deep, high-pressure pencil scoring creates sheer, stark graphite ledges that plunge into the surrounding void.

lighting.time: pale paper glare with heavy graphite core drop
lighting.why: Captures the stark contrast between the luminous off-white paper matrix and the dense, light-absorbing graphite shadow deposits.

concept.name: lens-medium
concept.fragment: LENS "medium": the artwork's MATERIAL AND MARKS become the island's physical character. Start from ANALYSIS.medium and ANALYSIS.palette, not from the subject. The ground is made of the marks: single-stroke ink becomes ribbon land and sweeping arcs of path with void where the paper is empty (shaper "ribbon", or "spiral" for a curl); airbrush gradients become soft radial terraces fading outward (shaper "radial"); fauvist or knife strokes become a patchwork of flat colour blocks at different heights (shaper "patchwork"); charcoal smudge becomes soft-edged dark masses with pale mist lying in the hollows (shaper "mound" or "basin"); pencil hatching or scratchy ink becomes angular slabs split by thin seams (shaper "shards"); vector doodles become dense small ornament on a tidy mirrored plan (shaper "symmetric"). Choose shaper params from the marks themselves (how many strokes, how wide, which way they sweep, how many blocks). Palette, surface_mix and cliff_treatment follow the medium (ink: paper-pale sand and ink-dark cliffs; airbrush: rings of surfaces fading by value; fauvist: saturated patches; charcoal: soft grey-green, mossy or soft cliffs). New props are the marks made solid: a brush flick as a curved blade of stone, a smudge as a low soft boulder, a doodle as a ring of beads, a knife stroke as a flat tilted slab. The figure's pose comes from how it is drawn (a single continuous stroke, a stack of colour patches), and it may be a monument of the marks rather than a living creature.
